lines.content: * This project is based on the [AddressBook-Level3](https://github.com/se-edu/addressbook-level3) project created by the [SE-EDU initiative](https://se-education.org). The architecture, the command and parser design and the testing approach are adapted from it.

* Libraries used: [JavaFX](https://openjfx.io/) (user interface), [Jackson](https://github.com/FasterXML/jackson) (JSON storage), [commonmark-java](https://github.com/commonmark/commonmark-java) (showing the bundled User Guide in the Help window), [JUnit5](https://github.com/junit-team/junit5) (testing), [Monocle](https://github.com/TestFX/Monocle) (running the user interface tests without a screen), [Checkstyle](https://checkstyle.sourceforge.io/) and [JaCoCo](https://www.jacoco.org/jacoco/) (code quality and coverage).
* Documentation is built with [MarkBind](https://markbind.org/) and the diagrams are drawn with [PlantUML](https://plantuml.com/).

The ***Architecture Diagram*** given above explains the high-level design of the App.
The following provides a quick overview of the main components and their interactions.

**`Main`** (consisting of classes [`Main`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F15-1/tp/tree/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/Main.java) and [`MainApp`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F15-1/tp/tree/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/MainApp.java)) is in charge of the app launch and shut down.
* At app launch, it initializes the other components in the correct sequence, and connects them up with each other.
* At shut down, it shuts down the other components and invokes cleanup methods where necessary.
The bulk of the app's work is done by the following four components:
* [**`Model`**](#model-component): Holds the data of the App in memory.
* [**`Storage`**](#storage-component): Reads data from, and writes data to, the hard disk.
[**`Commons`**](#common-classes) represents a collection of classes used by multiple other components.
**How the architecture components interact with each other**
The *Sequence Diagram* below shows how the components interact with each other for the scenario where the user issues the command `delete 1`.
Each of the four main components (also shown in the diagram above),
* defines its *API* in an `interface` with the same name as the Component.
* provides its functionality through a concrete `{Component Name}Manager` class that implements the corresponding API interface.

For example, the `Logic` component defines its API in `Logic.java` and implements it in `LogicManager.java`. Other components interact with a component through its interface rather than its concrete class, preventing them from coupling to that component's implementation, as illustrated in the following partial class diagram.
The sections below give more details of each component.
The **API** of this component is specified in [`Ui.java`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F15-1/tp/tree/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/ui/Ui.java)

The UI consists of a `MainWindow` and its parts, such as `CommandBox`, `ResultDisplay`, `PersonListPanel`, and `StatusBarFooter`. All of these, including `MainWindow`, inherit from the abstract `UiPart` class, which captures common behavior among classes that represent visible GUI parts.

`CommandBox` also lets the user step through the commands entered in the session with the `Up` and `Down` keys. The steps are kept by `CommandHistory`, a plain class with no JavaFX dependency, so it can be unit tested. It keeps the latest 100 commands, ignores blank commands and a repeat of the previous command, and remembers what the user had typed before stepping back so that `Down` returns to it. A command is recorded when it is entered, whether it succeeds or not. A failed command is left in the text field, and `CommandHistory` does not offer it again on the first `Up`, because it is already shown. A clear button overlays the right edge of the text field only while it contains text; it clears the text and returns focus without executing a command.

`CommandAssist` is the shared layer for the student-card shortcuts. It formats drafts using `CliSyntax` prefixes and command words, writes them through the small `CommandDraftTarget` interface implemented by `CommandBox`, and never calls `Logic`. `PersonCard` only reports the card's displayed index and the chosen field; it does not construct command strings or change model data. Field-editing mode is closed through a callback owned by `CommandAssist`, so a successful command, a new action on another card, and a change to the displayed list all leave the card and command box in a consistent state. `CommandBox` exposes the current draft and focus operations through `CommandDraftTarget`, and its clear control is a separate button layered over the text field rather than part of the command text.

The card's action buttons are rendered from `PersonListCard.fxml`. The subject pencil is added to the same `FlowPane` as the subject labels so it follows the final subject; it is not a separate row. Cancel is shown beside the card-level Edit control only during field-editing mode. All action buttons have accessible names and tooltips, and the card itself is focus-traversable so the actions can be reached without a mouse. Hover, keyboard focus and a one-tap touch fallback reveal the card actions.

The shortcut draft uses the same displayed index as the indexed commands. `PersonListPanel` observes its filtered list; when that list changes, an unchanged prepared draft is cleared and field-editing mode is closed, because the old number could now identify another student. A draft that the user edited is kept, as required for predictable cancellation. `CommandAssist` also prints `help COMMAND` to standard output for each shortcut, allowing the existing help command to own the usage text instead of duplicating it in the UI.

All subject values entered through commands go through `ParserUtil#parseSubject`. It normalizes the text, capitalizes the first Unicode letter with an uppercase mapping under `Locale.ROOT`, and then creates the immutable `Subject`. This keeps `add`, `edit`, lesson subject selection and subject filters consistent. Stored values loaded by `Subject` and `JsonAdaptedSubject` keep their original case, so existing data files and historical lessons are not rewritten.

The `UI` component uses the JavaFX UI framework. The layouts of these UI parts are defined in matching `.fxml` files in `src/main/resources/view`. For example, [`MainWindow.fxml`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F15-1/tp/tree/master/src/main/resources/view/MainWindow.fxml) specifies the layout of [`MainWindow`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F15-1/tp/tree/master/src/main/java/seedu/address/ui/MainWindow.java).
* executes user commands using the `Logic` component.
* listens for changes to `Model` data so that the UI can be updated with the modified data.
* keeps a reference to the `Logic` component, because the `UI` relies on the `Logic` to execute commands.
* depends on some classes in the `Model` component because it displays `Person` objects from the model.

1. When `Logic` is called upon to execute a command, the command is passed to an `AddressBookParser` object, which in turn creates a parser that matches the command (e.g., `DeleteCommandParser`) and uses it to parse the command.
1. This results in a `Command` object (more precisely, an object of one of its subclasses e.g., `DeleteCommand`) which is executed by the `LogicManager`.
1. The command can communicate with the `Model` when it is executed (e.g. to delete a person).
Note that although this is shown as a single step in the diagram above for simplicity, the code can require several interactions between the command object and the `Model` to complete the operation.
1. The result of the command execution is encapsulated as a `CommandResult` object which is returned from `Logic`.
Here are the other classes in `Logic` (omitted from the class diagram above) that are used for parsing a user command:

* When called upon to parse a user command, the `AddressBookParser` class creates an `XYZCommandParser` (`XYZ` is a placeholder for the specific command name, e.g., `AddCommandParser`). The parser uses the other classes shown above to parse the user command and create an `XYZCommand` object (e.g., `AddCommand`). The `AddressBookParser` returns that object as a `Command` object.

* All `XYZCommandParser` classes, such as `AddCommandParser` and `DeleteCommandParser`, implement the `Parser` interface so they can be treated similarly where appropriate, for example during testing.

* Arguments are parsed by each `XYZCommandParser`, not by `AddressBookParser`, because the prefixes, required fields and error messages differ between commands. Logic that more than one parser needs lives in shared classes instead of being copied:
* `ArgumentTokenizer`, `ArgumentMultimap` and `ParserUtil` split and validate prefixed values, and all prefixes are defined once in `CliSyntax`.
* An index that is not a positive whole number is reported as `Invalid command format!` with the command's usage. A parser gets this by calling `ParserUtil.parseIndex(value, usage)`.

* `CommandInput` splits the first word from the rest of an input and lower-cases that word, so command words and sub-command words do not depend on letter case. The same holds for the `confirm` keyword, which `ConfirmableIndex`, `ClearCommandParser`, `DemoCommandParser` and `LessonSeriesCancelCommandParser` compare ignoring case. Prefixes such as `n/` remain case-sensitive. `AddressBookParser` uses it for the command word, and `SubCommandParser` uses it for the sub-command word of `lesson` and `task`, and `PayCommandParser` and `ChargeCommandParser` for `pay list`, `pay reverse` and `charge reverse`. `SubCommandParser` is given one `Parser` per sub-command word, so adding a sub-command means registering one more parser.

* `ConfirmableIndex` parses an index with an optional `confirm` keyword and is used by `delete`, `task delete` and `hw delete`. It strips surrounding whitespace with `String.strip()` and splits the words with `(?U)\s+`, so all three treat Unicode spaces such as U+3000 the same way as ASCII ones, both around the arguments and between the index and `confirm`.

* Each prefix-based parser calls `ArgumentMultimap#verifyNoUnexpectedPrefixes` before required-prefix, duplicate and value checks. The multimap compares unaccepted prefix-shaped tokens with the prefixes its tokenizer accepted and with known parameter names. Names, venues and descriptions are not exempt from the retired `a/`, so its venue hint is shown. A typo such as `name/` is also reported instead of being absorbed. Notes, feedback, reasons and remarks are fully permissive because they may quote a command. A description tolerates an unaccepted short prefix such as `p/3` as prose. The fixed whitelist keeps `c/o`, `d/o`, `s/o`, `n/a` and `w/o` valid. A real prefix used by another command and an upper-case spelling are reported by name rather than as a misleading field or missing-prefix error. `AddressBookParser` also rejects the retired `a/` for index-only subcommands such as `pay reverse`, `hw delete`, `task done` and `lesson missed`, which do not tokenize prefixes. `find a/Home` remains a plain search for that text.

* stores the address book data i.e., all `Person` objects, each of which represents a student with a name, phone number, level, subjects and rate, and optionally an email, a venue and a remark (the `Person` objects are contained in a `UniquePersonList` object). Two `Person` objects are the same student if they have the same phone number and the same name, ignoring case.

* stores the `Lesson` objects, each of which is a lesson with a student, a subject, a date, a start time, a duration, a status and optionally a venue (the `Lesson` objects are contained in a `UniqueLessonList` object). A `Lesson` refers to its student by the student's name and phone number, which together identify a `Person`. Deleting a student deletes their lessons, and editing the name or phone number of a student keeps their lessons attached.

* stores immutable `LedgerEntry` records for lesson charges, student payments, withdrawals and the reversals of charges or payments. Each record refers to a permanent student UUID and, for charges and charge reversals, a lesson UUID; a reversal also refers to the entry it cancels. `Ledger` derives balances and unpaid dues from those records; those calculations do not mutate the ledger.

* stores the `Person` objects selected by the current filter, such as search results, in a separate _filtered_ list. It exposes this list as an unmodifiable `ObservableList<Person>` that the UI can observe and bind to, so the UI updates when the list changes.
* stores a `UserPrefs` object that represents the user’s preferences (currently, just the GUI settings). This is exposed to the outside as a `ReadOnlyUserPrefs` object.
* does not depend on any of the other three components (as the `Model` represents data entities of the domain, they should make sense on their own without depending on other components)
* can save both address book data and user preference data in JSON format, and read them back into corresponding objects.
* is implemented by `StorageManager`, which delegates the actual JSON file access to `JsonAddressBookStorage` and `JsonUserPrefsStorage` (one class per data file).
* saves the students and the lessons in the same data file. A data file written before lessons existed has no lesson list, and still loads with no lessons.
* depends on some classes in the `Model` component (because the `Storage` component's job is to save/retrieve objects that belong to the `Model`)
Classes used by multiple components are in the `seedu.address.commons` package.
This section describes some noteworthy details on how certain features are implemented.
### Student lookup and correction of optional values
`NameContainsKeywordsPredicate` normalizes names and keywords to NFC and applies the same per-code-point case
equivalence as `String.equalsIgnoreCase` before substring matching: `toUpperCase`, then `toLowerCase`.
This follows `Person#hasIdentity`, including dotless i and supplementary letters, while retaining significant
accents. It does not implement full Unicode case folding or multi-character mappings.
`StudentSummaryLabels` groups the full student list, including archived students, by case-insensitive name
once per textual summary. It precomputes labels by student ID, avoiding a student-list scan for each homework
row. Same-name students show only the last four phone digits. If those digits also collide, an eight-character
student-ID reference is added, falling back to the complete ID if its prefix collides. Archived status is part
of the same label. `Ledger` dues, `HomeworkQueries` and the `view` heading use these labels independently of
the current filter. This formatter is scoped to textual summaries, not contact cards or exports. Full contact
details remain in the explicit student overview, not in homework or dues rows or the startup dashboard.
`EditPersonDescriptor` distinguishes an omitted optional contact field from a requested clear using explicit
email and venue clear flags. The parser sets these only for an empty `e/` or `v/`; non-empty replacements
still pass normal validation. Copies, equality and hashes retain the clear intent. `EditCommand` replaces the
student with the same ID, so existing lesson snapshots and linked homework, ledger and tasks are retained.
An explicitly empty homework `f/` calls `Homework#withoutFeedback`, which returns a copy with absent feedback
and the same identity, due date and status. Clearing is also allowed after a status correction to `assigned`;
recording non-empty feedback still requires submission. No data-schema change is needed: absent email, venue
and feedback already use the existing optional JSON fields. Regression tests cover saving and reloading them.
### Lesson scheduling, agenda and conflict detection

The lesson commands are `lesson add`, `lesson repeat`, `lesson list`, `lesson move`, `lesson cancel`, `lesson done` and `lesson missed`. They share the `lesson` command word, which `AddressBookParser` hands to `LessonCommandParser`. That parser reads the next word and passes the rest of the arguments to the parser of that command. `agenda` is its own command word.

The sequence diagram below shows the successful changed-data path for `execute("lesson move 1 d/2026-12-24")`. It focuses on the Logic component; parser internals and the internal workings of Model and Storage are omitted. The command resolves the displayed index, validates and replaces the lesson, and reports overlaps without blocking the move. `LogicManager` then refreshes changed lesson numbers once and saves the updated data before returning success. A save failure retains the in-memory change and asks the tutor to retry `save`.
![Lesson rescheduling through Logic, with Model and Storage shown as black boxes](images/LessonMoveSequenceDiagram.svg)

Diagram source: [LessonMoveSequenceDiagram.puml](diagrams/LessonMoveSequenceDiagram.puml). Regenerate the SVG with `java -jar plantuml.jar -tsvg -o ../images docs/diagrams/LessonMoveSequenceDiagram.puml` from the repository root.

* **Lesson indices.** `Model#getFilteredLessonList()` returns the lessons that `agenda` or `lesson list` last chose, sorted by date, then start time, then student name. Lesson mutations retain the active filter. `LogicManager` compares the displayed identities and rows before and after a mutation and appends the refreshed numbered list when those rows change. Commands do not append a second list; `lesson add` marks its already-formatted list with `CommandResult#withDisplayedLessons`, so the central handler can reuse it. This prevents both stale numbers and duplicate numbering messages.

* **Overlaps.** `Lesson#overlaps(Lesson)` is true when both lessons are scheduled, are on the same date, and each starts before the other ends. It compares minutes since the start of the day, so back-to-back lessons are not an overlap and a lesson that ends at midnight can still be compared. `Model#getConflictingLessons(Lesson)` returns the other lessons that overlap a lesson, and `lesson add` and `lesson move` append the result to their message as a warning. `agenda` marks every lesson that has at least one overlap.

* **Cancelling.** `Lesson#cancel(String)` returns a copy with the status `CANCELLED` and the reason. The lesson is kept, so it stays in the agenda for billing, but it is no longer scheduled and so it never overlaps.
* **Immutability.** `Lesson` is immutable. `lesson move` and `lesson cancel` build a changed copy and ask the model to replace the old lesson with it, in the same way that `edit` replaces a `Person`.
* **Defaults to type less.** `lesson add` takes the subject from the student when the student has only one, uses 60 minutes if no duration is given, and uses the student's venue if no venue is given.

`travel buffer/MINUTES` updates the buffer through `Model#setTravelBuffer`. The value belongs to the `AddressBook`, so snapshots, resets and JSON saves include it. Missing values in older files default to 30; invalid stored values reject the file rather than silently altering the setting.

`TravelGap#find` sorts scheduled lessons chronologically and scans groups sharing a date and start time. It retains the latest preceding end and its tied lessons, so a short lesson nested inside a longer lesson cannot produce a misleading departure time. It uses minutes since midnight, avoiding wraparound at 00:00. Different dates and non-scheduled lessons are excluded. The command layer formats the returned gaps with the shared `MESSAGE_TRAVEL_WARNING`, including both student names, without changing lesson filters or blocking bookings. `AgendaCommand`, `TodayCommand`, `LessonAddCommand` and `LessonMoveCommand` use the same calculation. Add and move report only journeys into or out of the changed lesson; agenda and today restrict destinations to their displayed dates. Today's warnings use the same two-space indentation as its lesson rows.

`lesson series cancel LESSON_INDEX confirm` requires exact confirmation before resolving the occurrence in the displayed list. The optional UUID returned by `Lesson#getSeriesId` identifies its series independently of dates, and is retained by rescheduling, status updates, preparation updates and student edits. The command selects only scheduled occurrences whose date and time are not before its injected clock, builds all cancellations in an `AddressBook` copy, then replaces the model data once. The cancellation reason is `Series cancelled`; historical records and permanent IDs are retained. The series ID is an optional JSON field, so older lessons still load without being assigned to an invented series.

`LessonRepeatCommand` creates one UUID and attaches it to every occurrence using `Lesson#withSeries(UUID)`. `Lesson#getSeriesId` returns that optional UUID; `JsonAdaptedLesson` uses the same optional `seriesId` JSON field as recurring bookings. After adding the series, the command reports each travel gap involving a new occurrence once, including journeys into and out of it. Weekly agenda warnings are formatted inside the day loop, immediately after that day's lesson rows.

Move, single cancellation and series cancellation use `LessonCommandUtil#requireNotCharged` to retain billed history. Series cancellation validates every affected occurrence before building its replacement, so a charge on even the last eligible occurrence leaves all bookings and ledger records unchanged. Cancellation is a status change, not a deletion or clear, so it is outside the one-action undo scope described below and is not undoable.

`TravelGapTest`, `TravelCommandParserTest`, `LessonSeriesCancelCommandTest` and `LessonTravelWorkflowTest` cover buffer boundaries, venue exceptions, latest-end selection, moved occurrences, confirmation, filtered numbering, failed-save retries and JSON restarts.
**Aspect: how a lesson refers to its student**
* **Alternative 1 (current choice):** store the student's name and phone number in the lesson.
* Pros: The saved file stays flat and a lesson can be validated without loading students. A name and phone number already identify a student in TutorFlow.
* Cons: `AddressBook` must update the lessons when it edits or deletes a student. This is done in `setPerson` and `removePerson`, so no command has to remember it.
* **Alternative 2:** store a reference to the `Person` object.
* Pros: No update is needed when a student is edited.
* Cons: `Person` is immutable and is replaced on every edit, so the reference would have to be replaced as well, and the saved file would need ids that students do not have.
**Aspect: what to do when lessons overlap**
* **Alternative 1 (current choice):** warn, but still schedule or move the lesson.
* Pros: A tutor may double book on purpose, for example for a make-up lesson or two siblings. Blocking would force the tutor to delete a real lesson to record another.
* Cons: A warning in the result box is easy to miss, so `agenda` also marks overlapping lessons.
* Cons: This is overzealous validation and has no workaround.

Every date typed by the user is read by `ParserUtil.parseDate`, which resolves `today` and `tmr` against the injected clock and gives anything else to the `LessonDate` constructor. `LessonDate` hands the text to `FlexibleDateParser`, which splits it into three parts with the same separator (`/`, `-`, `.` or a space) between them and reads the parts as day, month and year, or as year, month and day. The month is one or two digits or an English month name, and the year is four digits or two digits for 2000 to 2099. Dates saved in the data file are always `YYYY-MM-DD`, written by `LessonDate#toStorageString`, and `JsonAdaptedLesson` only accepts that format when loading.

A date with a four-digit year has one reading. When the first and the last part both have at most two digits, as in `26-12-22`, `FlexibleDateParser` reads the day first (26 December 2022). It reads the year first only if the day-first reading is not a real date, as in `35-12-31`. The reading never depends on today's date.
**Alternative 1 (current choice):** read a date with two short end parts day first, and use the year-first reading only if that day does not exist.
* Pros: one rule, matching how dates are usually written in Singapore, and the same text always means the same date. It still accepts `35-12-31` as 31 December 2035.
* Cons: a year-first form such as `26-12-22` means 26 December 2022. The User Guide says to write a year-first date with four digits.
**Alternative 2:** take the reading nearer to today.
* Cons: it silently misreads ordinary day-first dates such as `26/11/27` and changes its result with the computer's date.
**Alternative 3:** refuse a date that can be read two ways, as `9/10` is refused.
* Cons: most two-digit dates in the next few years would be refused, because they can be read both ways.

`lesson done INDEX [n/NOTES]` is routed through `LessonCommandParser` to `LessonDoneCommandParser`. The parser validates the lesson index, rejects repeated `n/` prefixes and uses `ParserUtil#parseNotes` to normalise and validate optional notes. `Lesson` validates notes again at the model boundary, and `JsonAdaptedLesson` rejects invalid saved notes with an `IllegalValueException`.

`LessonDoneCommand` uses the current filtered lesson list, rejects cancelled lessons and dates after the local current date, then replaces the lesson with the immutable copy returned by `Lesson#complete`. A `Clock` can be injected into the command to test date boundaries without changing the system clock. Completing a lesson does not reset the active filter, so it can disappear from an upcoming-only list; `lesson list st/INDEX all/` includes completed lessons for later note corrections.

When notes are supplied again on a completed lesson, they replace the existing notes without creating another lesson. Omitting notes preserves them. The existing `LogicManager` save path persists the status and notes before returning success, and `view` includes these notes and the completed-lesson count.

`lesson missed INDEX` is routed through `LessonCommandParser` to `LessonMissedCommandParser`. It accepts only a positive lesson index, with no extra parameters. `LessonMissedCommand` resolves this index against the current filtered lesson list, rejects cancelled and completed lessons, and checks that the date is not later than the local current date. Like the completion command, it accepts an injected `Clock` for deterministic date-boundary tests.

The command replaces a scheduled lesson with the immutable copy returned by `Lesson#miss`, which retains all booking details, notes and identity fields. Repeating it on an already-missed lesson returns an informative message without replacing the record. Existing lesson filters, overlap checks, `view` history counts and JSON storage already support `LessonStatus.MISSED`; no new storage format is needed. A missed lesson can disappear from an upcoming-only filter, but remains accessible with `lesson list st/INDEX all/`. The existing `lesson done` command can correct a missed status to completed. `lesson move` rejects a missed lesson, because the moved copy would keep `MISSED` on its new date and the record of the missed slot would be lost. A make-up lesson is scheduled with `lesson add` instead.

`LessonMissedIntegrationTest` exercises command parsing, status changes, student history and JSON reload together. It also verifies that invalid arguments, invalid indices and rejected status/date changes leave the saved file unchanged.
### Weekly lesson series and back-dated lessons

`lesson repeat` (user story 9) and the `past/` flag of `lesson add` (user story 8) are routed through `LessonCommandParser` like the other lesson commands. `LessonRepeatCommandParser` tokenises the lesson prefixes together with `count/` and `every/`, and also tokenises `past/` so that it can reject it with a clear message, because a series starts today or later. It reads `count/` and `every/` with one pattern check, at most 3 digits, before parsing, so a huge or non-numeric value is rejected as a range error and cannot overflow.

The sequence diagram below shows `execute("lesson repeat st/1 d/2026-10-29 t/16:00 count/4")`. The parser creates the command, and the command then builds the four lessons, checks every one of them for duplicates and overlaps, and only then adds them to the model.
<puml src="diagrams/LessonRepeatSequenceDiagram.puml" alt="Interactions Inside the Logic and Model Components for the `lesson repeat` Command" />

`LessonRepeatCommand` builds every occurrence first, one per week (or every `every/` weeks) from the start date, and each is a normal `Lesson` made with `snapshotStudent`, so it records the student's id and academic level as `lesson add` does. All occurrences share one `seriesId`. The command then checks every occurrence against the existing lessons, and adds none of them if any is a duplicate. The adding itself is wrapped so that, if the model throws part-way, the occurrences added so far are deleted again. This makes the series all or nothing. An overlapping occurrence only produces a warning, which is listed for up to three occurrences and then summarised in one line. The command reports whether the displayed lesson list renumbered by comparing the displayed lessons before and after, not by guessing from the size of the list.

**The series id.** `Lesson` has an optional `seriesId` (a `UUID`, null when the lesson is not part of a series). It is copied by every method that returns a changed copy (`reschedule`, `cancel`, `complete`, `miss`, `prepare`, `withStudent`, `snapshotStudent`), so an occurrence stays in its series when it is moved or its status changes, and a later series cancel command can find every occurrence. `JsonAdaptedLesson` saves it as an optional field, so a data file written before series existed still loads. A `seriesId` that is present but is not a valid UUID, including a blank one, is rejected with `Lesson's seriesId is not a valid ID.`

**Dates.** `LessonCommandUtil` holds the date and subject checks that `lesson add`, `lesson repeat` and `lesson move` share: `requireNotInPast`, `requireNotAfterToday`, `requireNotTooFarPast`, `requireNearFuture` and `chooseSubject`. The date checks have a version that takes a `Clock`, and `LessonAddCommand` and `LessonRepeatCommand` have a constructor that takes one, in the same way as `LessonDoneCommand`, so that the boundaries (today, two years ahead and two years back) can be tested with a fixed date. With `past/`, a date after today is rejected, so that `past/` cannot create a scheduled lesson that `lesson done` would refuse.

**Travel warnings.** After scheduling, the shared travel-gap calculation reports journeys into or out of the new occurrences without blocking them. It excludes unrelated journeys and emits each affected journey once.

`LessonRepeatCommandTest`, `LessonRepeatCommandParserTest` and `SeriesIntegrationTest` cover the series rules, the all-or-nothing behaviour, moving and cancelling an occurrence, and saving and reloading a series.
**Aspect: how to make a series all or nothing**
* **Alternative 1 (current choice):** check every occurrence first, then add them and delete the added ones again if adding fails.
* Pros: No partial series is ever visible to the tutor, and the check catches every duplicate before anything changes.
* Cons: The rollback is written by hand in the command, because the model has no transaction.
* **Alternative 2:** add the occurrences one by one and stop at the first failure.
* Cons: A tutor could be left with half a series and have to find and delete it.

`today` shows the dashboard, which answers "what does today require?", and `view INDEX` shows the overview of one student. Both are read-only commands that return their whole result as text for the result box.

**Parsing.** `today` takes no parameters, so `AddressBookParser` calls `requireNoArguments` before it creates the command: `today 2` fails with `The 'today' command takes no parameters.` instead of running. `AddressBookParser` passes `LocalDate.now()` to `TodayCommand`, and `ViewCommandParser` passes it to `ViewCommand` with the parsed index. The commands do not read the clock themselves, so tests can give them a fixed date.

### Undo of the latest deletion or clear

Undo is deliberately a single-action, session-only safety net, not a general undo history. It restores the whole address book from immediately before the latest successful `delete`, `hw delete`, `task delete` or `clear confirm`. It does not undo lesson cancellations, edits, payments or other commands.
`VersionedAddressBook` extends `AddressBook` with three pieces of state:
* `transitionState` is a snapshot taken before a destructive command runs.
* `lastState` is the snapshot promoted from `transitionState` only after that command succeeds.
* `lastDestructiveAction` is the message fragment used by `UndoCommand`.

`LogicManager` calls `Model#beforeCommand(boolean)` before command execution and `Model#afterCommand(String, boolean)` in its `finally` path. The boolean tells the model whether the parsed command extends `DestructiveCommand`; the description comes from `DestructiveCommand#getDestructDescription()`. A failed command discards `transitionState`, leaving any earlier successful undo point available.

`UndoCommand` calls `Model#undoDestructiveAction()`, which restores `lastState` through `resetData`. The `LogicManager` then saves the restored state through the normal changed-data path. A save failure retains the restored in-memory state so `save` can retry, matching every other mutating command.

Only one undo point is retained. A successful non-destructive command clears it in `afterCommand`, as does a successful destructive command replacing it. This is intentional: undo must never silently roll back later work. Read-only commands do not clear it. The state is not persisted, so closing TutorFlow ends the undo opportunity.

`VersionedAddressBookTest` exercises the hooks and failed-destructive path directly. `UndoCommandTest` and `UndoIntegrationTest` cover the command and persistence behaviour. Future changes to command execution must keep `afterCommand` on the failure path; otherwise a rejected confirmation can consume the valid undo point.
`LedgerEntry` is immutable and records its UUID, permanent student UUID, optional lesson UUID, kind,

positive exact `BigDecimal` amount, date and notes. There are four kinds. `CHARGE` and `CHARGE_REVERSAL` require a lesson UUID; `PAYMENT` and `PAYMENT_REVERSAL` have none. A reversal also records the UUID of the entry it cancels (`reverses`), has the same student, lesson and amount as that entry, and can be added only once per entry. * **Mainstream OS**: Windows, Linux, Unix, or macOS
* **Tutor**: The user of TutorFlow, an independent private tutor who teaches multiple students
* **Student**: A person the tutor teaches, recorded with contact details, academic level, subjects, lesson rate and an optional usual venue
* **Level**: A student's academic level in the Singapore education system: `P1` to `P6` (primary), `S1` to `S5` (secondary) or `J1` to `J2` (junior college)
* **Rate**: The amount a student is charged for one hour of lesson, in Singapore dollars (SGD)
* **Duplicate student**: A student with the same name and phone number as another student, after ignoring letter case and extra spaces
* **Lesson**: A teaching session with one student, with a subject, date, start time, duration and venue
* **Lesson status**: The state of a lesson: _scheduled_ (has not happened yet), _completed_ (took place), _cancelled_ (called off in advance) or _missed_ (the student did not attend)
* **Overlap**: Two scheduled lessons on the same date whose time ranges share at least one minute. Lessons that end exactly when the next one starts do not overlap
* **Agenda**: A view of the tutor's lessons in time order for a day or a week
* **Dashboard**: The view shown on startup that lists what needs the tutor's attention today, such as today's lessons, lessons awaiting notes, overdue homework and outstanding payments
* **Student overview**: A single view of a student's details, next lesson, recent lesson notes, outstanding homework and unpaid balance
* **Lesson notes**: Free text that the tutor records about a lesson, such as what was covered and what the student needs to improve
* **Homework status**: The state of a homework item: _assigned_, _submitted_ or _reviewed_. Homework that is still assigned after its due date is _overdue_
* **Charge**: The fee for one completed lesson, calculated from the student's rate and the lesson duration unless the tutor specifies another amount
* **Payment**: Money received from a student, recorded against the student rather than against a particular lesson
* **Balance**: The total charges minus the total payments of a student. A positive balance is _outstanding_, and a negative balance means the student is _in credit_
* **Index**: The position of an item in the list currently shown on screen, used by commands to refer to that item
* **Prefix**: A short label ending in `/`, such as `n/` or `d/`, that marks the start of a command parameter
* **Data file**: The local file in which TutorFlow saves all of its data

### v1.4 continuity and domain extension contract
`Person.getId()` and `Lesson.getId()` are persisted UUIDs, distinct from visible indices and
from value equality. `Lesson.getStudentId()` links records across profile edits. Legacy lessons
are linked during loading; their missing academic level remains `Optional.empty()`. Newly
scheduled lessons use `snapshotStudent` exactly at creation. Reschedule, status changes,
preparation, profile edits, aggregate copying, and JSON round trips retain the historical level.
Archive and preparation participate in value equality, as does academic level; UUIDs do not.
Equal cancelled lessons remain separate records and exact-ID lookup chooses the edited record.
All domain extensions must update `ReadOnlyAddressBook`, `AddressBook.resetData` and its copy
constructor/equality, the real JSON root/adapters, and focused round-trip tests together.
`Storage.snapshotAddressBook` uses that exact persisted representation for dirty detection,
so UI-only equality must never decide whether a write is required. Schema 17 is written to
`tutorflow-v14.json`; `VersionedAddressBookStorage` reads legacy data only when the current
path is positively absent. The logic constructor's initial-save flag explicitly persists
migrated IDs even before a command mutates the model. Failed initial writes remain dirty.
The atomic writer creates only parent directories before its sibling temporary file. It never
precreates the current destination, so an interrupted first save leaves legacy fallback available
on restart. The storage writeSnapshot seam passes the actual serialized bytes to this writer.
Unreadable source protection is retained until positive absence or successful preservation.
`StorageSchema.MINIMUM_VERSION` and `CURRENT_VERSION` centralize the supported range (14 through 19 now).
The shared `tutorflow-v14.json` path stays fixed as later domains are added. Homework uses
schema 15, finance uses schema 16, follow-up tasks use schema 17, task payment links use schema 18 and withdrawals
use schema 19; the next domain must advance it to 20. Each build accepts unversioned legacy
data and versions 14 through its current version, with explicit defaults for missing older fields.
Add prior-version loading and future-version refusal tests alongside each schema increment.
Storage checks the raw JSON schema before binding current student/lesson fields. An unsupported
version produces `UnsupportedSchemaException` as the cause of `DataLoadingException`; `MainApp.init`
propagates it before constructing a model, logic, or UI. The original stays at its original path,
and storage refuses subsequent saves. Never route this exception through corruption recovery or
silently ignore newer domain fields. Users need a compatible binary or a matching backup.
A file that cannot be opened is not corrupt. `JsonAddressBookStorage#isAccessFailure` tells a failure
to open or read a file, which is an `IOException` that is not a `JsonProcessingException`, from
invalid content. Only invalid content is set aside. A file that another program holds, or that the
permissions forbid reading, can well be valid, so setting it aside would hide the records of a tutor,

start in the same way as for an unsupported schema, with a message that names the file and the
reason, and `JsonAddressBookStorage#requireOpenedSource` makes every save refuse to replace the file.
The next start that can open the file loads or migrates it.

For power-users, TutorFlow can help you manage your students and lessons faster than traditional GUI applications.
1. Ensure that Java `25` or later is installed on your computer.
**Mac users:** Ensure you have the precise JDK version prescribed [here](https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/javaInstallationMac.html).

Some example commands you can try:
* `add n/John Doe p/98765432 l/S4 s/Math r/50` : Adds a student named `John Doe`, who is in Secondary 4, learns Math and pays $50 per hour.

* Words in `UPPER_CASE` are the parameters to be supplied by the user.
For example, in `add n/NAME`, replace `NAME` with a value such as `John Doe`.
* Items in square brackets are optional.
For example, `n/NAME [e/EMAIL]` can be used as `n/John Doe e/john@example.com` or as `n/John Doe`.
* Items followed by `...` can appear zero or more times.
For example, `s/SUBJECT...` can be written as `s/Math` or `s/Math s/Physics`.
* Items such as `week/` and `all/` are flags: write them on their own, without a value.
For example, `agenda week/` is accepted, but `agenda week/yes` is rejected.
* Parameters can be in any order.
For example, if the command specifies `n/NAME p/PHONE_NUMBER`, `p/PHONE_NUMBER n/NAME` is also acceptable.
* `list` accepts academic filters and archive flags; invalid or extra arguments are rejected.
For example, `student list l/S4 s/Math` shows active S4 Math students.
* `today` and `exit` take no parameters. If you type anything after them, TutorFlow shows an error and does not run them.
For example, `exit now` is rejected, so a mistyped command cannot close the app.

* Command words are not case-sensitive: `LIST`, `List` and `list` are the same command, and so are `LESSON ADD` and `lesson add`. The same goes for the keyword `confirm`. Parameter prefixes such as `n/` and `st/` must still be in lower case, and the values you type keep their case.

* A mistyped parameter prefix is reported as `Unknown prefix for this command: name/.` instead of being absorbed into the previous value and blamed on that field. This includes a prefix that belongs to a different command, such as `amt/` in `lesson add`, and an upper-case spelling such as `N/`.

* Slash-bearing text is still allowed where it is ordinary content. A name or venue accepts `c/o`, `d/o`, `s/o`, `n/a`, `w/o` and `Blk/123`. Notes, feedback, reasons and remarks may quote a full command, including tokens such as `n/` or `desc/`. A description accepts an unaccepted short prefix such as `p/3` as prose, but still rejects a field-name spelling such as `name/` and the retired `a/`.

Every date parameter, such as `d/` in `lesson add`, `agenda` and `pay`, `due/` in `hw add` and `task add`, accepts the same ways of writing a date, so you can type the one you find quickest.
* The **day, month and year** are separated by `/`, `-`, `.` or a space, the same one between all three.
* The date is written **day first** or **year first**. A month is never written first, so `12/22/2026` is not accepted.
* The **month** is a number, such as `9` or `09`, or its English name in full or short, such as `Sep`, `Sept` or `September`, in any letter case.
* The **year** has four digits, or two digits for a year from 2000 to 2099. A two-digit year is read last when that makes a real date, or first when it does not.
* `today` and `tmr` also work wherever a date is accepted, in any letter case.
* A date that does not exist, such as `30/02/2026`, is rejected. It is never moved to a nearby date.

For a JAR, rebuild with `./gradlew shadowJar` or download an updated release, then restart with that JAR. `Reload guide` does not download newer documentation into an older JAR.

Format: `add n/NAME p/PHONE_NUMBER l/LEVEL s/SUBJECT... r/RATE [e/EMAIL] [v/VENUE]`

* `NAME` is 1-100 printable characters after trimming and must contain at least one letter. It may contain letters in any language (such as `José Álvarez` or `陈伟明`), digits, spaces and `. , ' ( ) / - @`, such as `Tan Wei Ming (twin A)`, `Priya d/o Kumar` or `John @ Tan`. It does not matter how an accent is typed, so `José` written with one character and with a letter and a separate accent is the same name. Avoid typing a `/` right after a space when it would look like a prefix, such as `s/o`, because TutorFlow reads it as the start of the next parameter.

* `NAME` and `VENUE` reject a field-name typo such as `name/` or `email/` instead of absorbing it into the value. Ordinary relationship or address forms such as `s/o`, `d/o`, `c/o`, `n/a`, `w/o` and `Blk/123` remain valid.
* `LEVEL` is one of `P1` to `P6` (primary), `S1` to `S5` (secondary) or `J1` to `J2` (junior college). It is not case-sensitive, so `s3` is the same as `S3`.

* `PHONE_NUMBER` has 8 to 15 digits and can start with `+`, for example `91234567` or `+6591234567`. Spaces and hyphens between the digits are allowed and are removed, so `9123 4567` is stored as `91234567`.

* `SUBJECT` is free text of up to 30 letters in any language, digits, spaces, `&` and `-`, such as `Math`, `English & Literature` or `华文`. Subjects are not case-sensitive. When you enter one, its first letter is capitalized automatically, so `math` is saved and shown as `Math`. The rest of what you type keeps its case.
* `RATE` is the amount charged per hour in SGD, from `0` to `9999.99` with at most 2 decimal places. A leading `$` is accepted, so `50`, `50.00` and `$50` are the same rate.
* `VENUE` is where the student is usually taught, up to 100 characters.

* The old address prefix `a/` is no longer supported. Use `v/` for a student's venue, such as `v/2902 Yishun`. An `a/` parameter is rejected as an unknown prefix instead of being read as part of the preceding email or venue.

* A mistyped prefix such as `name/`, `phone/`, `sub/`, `email/` or `venue/` is named in an `Unknown prefix for this command` error. Correct the spelling instead of looking for a fault in the preceding field.
* Extra spaces in a `NAME` are ignored, so `John  Tan` is stored as `John Tan`.
* A student can have at most 10 different subjects, so a command with more than 10 `s/SUBJECT` values is rejected. The same limit applies when you [edit](#editing-a-student-edit) a student.
* Two students are duplicates if they have the same phone number and a name that matches when letter case and extra spaces are ignored. A duplicate is not added.

* Two different students can share a name, for example two students called `Tan Wei Ming` with different phone numbers. TutorFlow adds the student and shows a note, so that you can spot a double entry.
**Tip:** A student must have between 1 and 10 subjects. The email and the venue are optional.
* `add n/John Doe p/98765432 l/S4 s/Math r/50`
* `add n/Betsy Crowe p/98761234 l/J1 s/Physics s/Chemistry r/62.50 e/betsycrowe@example.com v/Blk 123 Bishan St 13`

It shows the student's name, phone number, linked counts and, if there are any, a warning about upcoming lessons and commitments, and asks you to repeat the command with `confirm`.

* The order is saved, so it is still used the next time you open the app. Until you first use `sort`, new students are added at the end of the list.

Schedules a lesson for a student.
* `STUDENT_INDEX` is the index number shown in the displayed student list, and **must be a positive integer** 1, 2, 3, ...

* `DATE` is written in any of the [ways to write a date](#writing-dates), such as `2026-12-22`, `22/12/2026` or `22 Dec 26`, or as the word `today` or `tmr` (tomorrow), in any letter case, which TutorFlow works out from the date on your computer. It must be today or later, and no more than 2 years ahead, which catches a mistyped year.

* `past/` is a flag that records a lesson that has **already taken place**, so that you can complete it and bill it. With `past/`, a date before today is accepted, up to 2 years ago, but a date after today is rejected, so use `past/` only for a lesson that has already taken place. Without it, a date in the past is rejected, because that is usually a mistyped year. Every other rule still applies.

* Each lesson remembers the student's **level at the time of booking**, so that `lesson list` can still show it after the student moves up a level. Lessons that were booked before this version show `unknown (not recorded)`.
* `TIME` is written in 24-hour time, such as `16:30`. `4:30pm` and `1630` are also accepted.
* `MINUTES` is the length of the lesson, from `15` to `480` in steps of `15`. If it is left out, it is `60`.
* `SUBJECT` must be one of the student's subjects, and is not case-sensitive. If the student has only one subject, it can be left out. If the student has several, it must be given.
* `VENUE` is up to 100 characters. If it is left out, the student's usual venue is used, or `—` if the student has none.
* A lesson must end on the day it starts, so `t/23:00 dur/120` is rejected. Split it into two lessons.
* Two lessons are duplicates if they have the same student, subject, date, time and duration. A duplicate is rejected.

* Adding a lesson keeps the current day, week or student lesson filter. If the new lesson shifts existing lesson numbers, the result shows the complete current lesson list with fresh numbers. Use those numbers for your next lesson command.

**Overlaps only warn:** if the new lesson overlaps another scheduled lesson by at least one minute on the same date, it is still scheduled and the result lists the lessons it overlaps with. Lessons that end exactly when the next one starts do not overlap. Cancelled lessons are ignored.
* `lesson add st/1 s/Math d/2026-12-22 t/16:30 dur/90` Schedules a 90-minute Math lesson for the 1st student at the student's usual venue.
* `lesson add st/2 d/2026-12-23 t/19:00 v/Online` Schedules a 60-minute lesson online for the 2nd student, in the only subject that student takes.
* `lesson add st/2 d/tmr t/19:00 dur/60 v/Online` Schedules a lesson for tomorrow.
* `lesson add st/1 d/2026-10-12 t/16:30 past/` Records a lesson on 12 October 2026 that has already happened, even though that date is past.
Schedules the regular weekly lessons of a student in one command.
Format: `lesson repeat st/STUDENT_INDEX [s/SUBJECT] d/START_DATE t/TIME [dur/MINUTES] [v/VENUE] count/COUNT [every/WEEKS]`
* The student, subject, date, time, duration and venue are written as for [`lesson add`](#scheduling-a-lesson-lesson-add), except that `past/` is **not** accepted: a series starts today or later.
* A series cannot be scheduled for an **archived student**: restore the student first with `restore INDEX`, as for `lesson add`.

* `COUNT` is the number of lessons, from `2` to `52`. `WEEKS` is the gap between two lessons in weeks, from `1` to `12`; if `every/` is left out, it is `1`. Every lesson must fall within 2 years of today.
* The first lesson is on `START_DATE`. Each later lesson is at the same time of day, `WEEKS` weeks after the one before it.

* The series is **all or nothing**. TutorFlow checks every lesson first, and if any of them is invalid or is a duplicate of a lesson that already exists, it adds none of them and says `This exact lesson already exists. No occurrences were added.`
* Each lesson is a full, independent lesson: you can move, cancel, complete or bill it on its own. The lessons are linked only so that a series can be cancelled together.

* The new lessons are not added to the lesson list that is displayed, so run `agenda` or `lesson list st/STUDENT_INDEX` to see and number them. If adding the series changes the numbers on screen, the result ends with `Lesson numbers have changed. Current lesson list:` and the new numbering, as `lesson add` does.
* Lessons that overlap another lesson only produce a warning, as for `lesson add`. If many lessons of the series overlap, the warning is summarised in one line.
* `lesson repeat st/4 d/2026-10-29 t/16:00 count/4` Schedules four weekly lessons, starting on 29 October 2026.
* `lesson repeat st/1 d/tmr t/17:00 dur/90 count/10 every/2` Schedules ten lessons two weeks apart, starting tomorrow. The result says `Scheduled 10 occurrences, every 2 weeks.`

* With `week/`, it shows the Monday to Sunday week that contains the date, one day after another. A day without lessons shows `— no lessons —`.
* Each line shows the lesson number, the time, the student, the subject, the venue, and the status if the lesson is not simply scheduled. Lessons that overlap another lesson are marked `⚠ overlaps`.
* Cancelled lessons are listed but are not counted in the number of lessons and the total time.
* The lesson numbers are the ones that `lesson move`, `lesson cancel`, `lesson done` and `lesson missed` take, so run `agenda` or `lesson list` first and then use the number you see.

* Lessons are numbered in time order. If moving, cancelling, completing or marking a lesson missed changes the displayed numbers, the result includes `Lesson numbers have changed. Current lesson list:` and the refreshed list. If every lesson keeps its number, for example when a lesson only changes its time or is cancelled but stays in the list, the numbers are not shown again. Use those new numbers for your next command. Running `agenda` or `lesson list` again also refreshes the list.
* A week with more than 200 lessons shows the first 200 rows and a line saying how many were omitted, so the result box stays responsive.
* A day without lessons is not an error: it shows `No lessons on Tue 22 Dec 2026.`
* `agenda d/2026-12-22 week/` Shows the week of Monday 21 December 2026.

* The first section, `TODAY'S LESSONS`, shows the number of lessons today and their total time, followed by the time, student, subject and venue of each lesson. Lessons that overlap another lesson are marked `⚠ overlaps`. Cancelled lessons are left out.

* All four sections are always shown. An empty section is not an error: it shows `No lessons today.`, `All past lessons are recorded.`, `No overdue homework.` or `No outstanding balances. Everyone is up to date.`
* To keep the result box responsive, each lesson section lists at most 200 rows. The heading still gives the complete count and total time.

### Listing the lessons of a student: `lesson list`
Shows the lessons of one student.
* `STUDENT_INDEX` is the index number shown in the displayed student list.
* By default, only upcoming lessons are shown, which means scheduled lessons from today onwards. With `all/`, past, completed, cancelled and missed lessons are shown as well.

* Each line ends with the student's level when the lesson was booked, such as `[Level at booking: S3]`, and the status. A lesson that was booked before this was recorded shows `[Level at booking: unknown (not recorded)]`.
* The lessons are numbered in date order. These are the numbers that `lesson move`, `lesson cancel`, `lesson done` and `lesson missed` take.
* `lesson list st/1` Shows the upcoming lessons of the 1st student.
* `lesson list st/1 all/` Shows every lesson of the 1st student.
Moves a lesson to another date, time, duration or venue, and keeps everything else.
* `INDEX` is the lesson number in the list that is currently shown by `agenda` or `lesson list`, and **must be a positive integer** 1, 2, 3, ...
* At least one of the optional fields must be given. Fields that are not given stay as they were.

* The values follow the same rules as for [`lesson add`](#scheduling-a-lesson-lesson-add). A new date must be today or later. Only a date that you give is checked, so you can still change the time of a lesson that has already passed.

* A completed, cancelled or missed lesson cannot be rescheduled. Moving a missed lesson would lose the record that it was missed, so schedule a make-up lesson with [`lesson add`](#scheduling-a-lesson-lesson-add) instead.
* If the move makes the lesson identical to another lesson, it is rejected. If it makes the lesson overlap another lesson, it is moved and the result warns you.
* `lesson move 1 d/2026-12-24` Moves the 1st lesson to 24 December 2026 at the same time.
* `lesson move 2 t/17:00 v/Online` Moves the 2nd lesson to 17:00 and changes its venue to `Online`.
Cancels a lesson but keeps its record, so that you can still see that the slot was booked.
* `INDEX` is the lesson number in the list that is currently shown by `agenda` or `lesson list`.
* `REASON` is up to 200 characters on one line, such as `Student unwell`.
* The lesson stays in the agenda as cancelled and no longer overlaps other lessons.
* A lesson that is already cancelled or already completed cannot be cancelled.
* A cancelled lesson does not block its slot. To book that time again, use `lesson add` with the same details. The cancelled record stays in your history.
* A lesson that was marked missed can still be cancelled, for example to correct a booking that should never have counted. Its date, time, venue and notes are kept.
* A missed lesson with an active charge cannot be cancelled. Reverse the charge first with [`charge reverse`](#charging-a-lesson-charge).

**Cancelling a missed lesson replaces its missed record:** the lesson then counts as cancelled, not missed, in `view` and `lesson list`, and this cannot be undone. Only cancel a missed lesson if the "missed" was a mistake.
* `lesson cancel 3 r/Student unwell` Cancels the 3rd lesson and records the reason.
### Cancelling future occurrences of a series: `lesson series cancel`
Ends a recurring series without erasing its history.
* Select the displayed number of any occurrence belonging to the series, even a past occurrence.
* `confirm` is required, and can be written in any letter case. Without it, no lesson is changed.

* All scheduled occurrences starting now or later are cancelled together, including occurrences moved to another date or time. Occurrences that have started, or are already completed, missed or cancelled, remain unchanged.
* Each affected lesson keeps its identity and booking details, with the reason `Series cancelled`. No record is deleted.
* A lesson not linked to a recurring series is rejected. A series with no eligible occurrences is also rejected without changing data.
* Select an existing occurrence of the series. This command cancels existing recurring bookings; it does not create them.
* If any affected occurrence has a recorded charge, nothing is cancelled. Billed history is retained.
* Cancellation is a status change, not a deletion, and is not undoable. `confirm` is required because the change affects multiple bookings.
* Success is `Cancelled N series occurrences.` (or `Cancelled 1 series occurrence.` for a single occurrence).
Example: `lesson list st/1 all/`, then `lesson series cancel 3 confirm` cancels the eligible occurrences of the series containing the 3rd displayed lesson.
Sets one offline buffer for journeys between lessons at different physical venues. Warnings never block a booking and do not calculate routes or actual journey times.

* `MINUTES` must be a whole number from 0 to 180, inclusive. The default is 30 minutes; 0 disables travel warnings. The setting is saved and restored on reopening TutorFlow. Any other value, such as `buffer/200`, shows the command usage and changes nothing.

* Each scheduled lesson is compared with earlier scheduled lessons on the same date. The gap starts when the **latest-ending** earlier lesson ends, not necessarily the lesson that started most recently.

* A gap shorter than the buffer produces a warning naming both students, the venues, destination date and time, available minutes and required buffer. For example: `Travel warning: Tan Wei Ming at Bishan -> Priya Kumar at Clementi (Sat 24 Oct 2026 11:10): 10 min available; 30 min required.` Back-to-back lessons at different venues have a zero-minute gap and can therefore trigger a travel warning without overlapping.

* There is no travel warning for overlapping lessons, an unnamed venue, `Online` (ignoring case), or the same venue ignoring case. If several preceding lessons finish together, the first at a different physical venue is used.

* After `lesson add`, `lesson repeat` and `lesson move`, warnings cover journeys into or out of the added or moved lessons, not unrelated journeys on those dates. Warnings also appear below each day's relevant lessons in `agenda` and below today's lessons in `today`, and when you change the buffer, which lists the warnings on every date, including past ones. Changing the buffer does not change the currently displayed lesson numbers.

* To keep command results responsive, a single result shows at most 50 travel warnings. If more exist, the result says how many were shown and how many exist in total. The rest remain in the data and are shown by narrower agenda or lesson queries.
* `travel buffer/10` sets a ten-minute buffer and reports insufficient gaps.
* `travel buffer/0` disables travel warnings; overlap warnings still work.
### Completing a lesson and recording notes: `lesson done`
Marks a lesson completed and optionally records what was taught.
* `INDEX` is the lesson number from the current `agenda` or `lesson list`, not the student number. It must be a positive integer.

* The first completion adds the hourly lesson fee to the student’s balance and shows `Charge of $X.XX recorded.` Updating notes never charges again. A fee that is zero, including after cent rounding, completes the lesson without creating a charge and explains why: for a rate of $0.00 it says `No automatic charge: This student's rate is $0.00.` and how to specify an amount. Use [`charge`](#charging-a-lesson-charge) to bill a lesson by hand.
* Only lessons dated today or earlier can be completed, using your computer's local date. A cancelled lesson cannot be completed.

* `NOTES` is optional free text of 1–1000 printable characters on one line. Leading/trailing whitespace is trimmed and repeated spaces are collapsed. An empty `n/`, line breaks and repeated `n/` parameters are rejected.

* Completing a lesson retains its student, subject, date, time, duration and venue. The status and notes are saved automatically. Use `view STUDENT_INDEX` to see recent notes and the completed-lesson count.
* Repeating the command with `n/NOTES` updates the notes on the same completed lesson. Omitting `n/` retains existing notes. A lesson previously marked missed can also be changed to completed.
* A completed lesson disappears from an upcoming-only `lesson list`. Use `lesson list st/STUDENT_INDEX all/` to include it again; check the current lesson number before updating notes.
* A space followed by `n/` starts a note parameter, so it cannot also appear literally inside the note text.
* `agenda` followed by `lesson done 1` completes today's 1st lesson without adding notes.
* `lesson list st/1 all/` followed by `lesson done 2 n/Covered quadratic roots. Revise factorisation.` completes the 2nd displayed lesson or updates its notes if already completed.
Marks a scheduled lesson as missed without deleting its record.
* `INDEX` is the positive lesson number from the current `agenda` or `lesson list`, not the student number. Use `lesson list st/STUDENT_INDEX all/` to select a past lesson.
* Only lessons dated today or earlier can be marked missed, using your computer's local date. Future, cancelled and completed lessons are rejected without changing data.
* The student, subject, date, time, duration, venue and existing notes are retained. The missed status is saved automatically and counted in `view STUDENT_INDEX` under lesson history.
* A missed lesson disappears from an upcoming-only list and no longer counts as a scheduling overlap. Use `all/` to include it again and check its current lesson number.
* Repeating `lesson missed` on the same missed lesson leaves it unchanged. If the lesson actually took place, use `lesson done INDEX [n/NOTES]` to correct it to completed.

Reverses the latest deletion or clear made in this session.
* It applies to `delete`, `hw delete`, `task delete` and `clear confirm`; it does not restore lesson cancellations or other edits.

TutorFlow automatically saves after a command changes data. If saving fails, fix the reported problem and use `save` to retry before closing. Read-only commands do not write the data file.

Each save is written completely to a temporary file beside the data file before replacing the previous save. If writing fails, the previous saved contents remain intact. If your file system cannot replace files atomically, TutorFlow reports a save error; move the app to a local folder that supports atomic file replacement and retry.

If a change cannot be saved, for example because the disk is full or the file is read-only, TutorFlow says `Your change was applied in this session but could not be saved`, and the reason. The change is still in the running app, so fix the problem (free some space, or make the file writable) and run `save` to retry saving. Read-only commands do not write the data file. Closing TutorFlow with `exit`, the window close button, or File > Exit retries saving and is refused if saving still fails, so that you do not lose the change.
Read-only commands do not routinely save. After a failed save, they display an unsaved-changes reminder. Run `save` after fixing the problem; a successful retry clears that reminder.

TutorFlow data is saved automatically as a JSON file `data/tutorflow-v14.json` relative to the folder from which TutorFlow is launched. Advanced users are welcome to update data directly by editing that data file.

If your changes make the data file invalid, TutorFlow does not delete it. At the next run it renames the file to `tutorflow-v14.json.corrupt` (or `tutorflow-v14.json.corrupt.1` and so on, if that name is taken), starts with no students and lessons, and tells you where the file went. Fix the file and rename it back to `tutorflow-v14.json` while TutorFlow is closed to get your records back. We still recommend backing up the file before editing it.

If the original cannot be renamed (for example, while another program holds it open), saving is blocked and retries preservation before replacing it. The original bytes are retained in the `.corrupt` copy once the lock clears.

If TutorFlow cannot **open** the data file, for example because another program holds it open or you may not read it, the file can well be valid, so TutorFlow never renames it. It does not start: a window says why, nothing is changed, and nothing is saved over the file. Fix the problem and start TutorFlow again.

Furthermore, certain edits can cause TutorFlow to behave in unexpected ways (e.g., if a value entered is outside of the acceptable range). Therefore, edit the data file only if you are confident that you can update it correctly.
